title: Private upgrades: implement backup + restore hooks (storage backends + encryption)
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Context
Private upgrade workflow requires safe-by-default backups prior to any irreversible step (notably DB schema migrations / config state changes), plus deterministic restore hooks for rollback. This ticket implements the backup/restore hook contracts and orchestrator integration in redwood-private-installer, with coverage across key storage backends and explicit encryption requirements.

Goals
- Provide standard hook points for backups and restores that are invoked by the upgrade plan/state machine.
- Support both VPC and on-prem/air-gapped environments.
- Ensure backups are encrypted, verifiable, and auditable (manifest + timestamps + key IDs + checksums), and that restore verification is part of the workflow.
- Reduce support incidents by making failure modes explicit and blocking upgrades when backups are not possible.

Non-goals (for v1)
- Full point-in-time restore across every historical DB/version edge case.
- Automated multi-hop major-version upgrades that require complex data transformations.

Proposed scope / design
1) Hook contract (installer-facing)
- Hook phases (invoked from upgrade plan):
  - preflight.backup: validate backup destination reachable + credentials + enough headroom
  - backup.start: acquire lock / enter maintenance mode (as needed)
  - backup.snapshot: perform storage-layer snapshot(s) OR logical backup (depending on backend)
  - backup.verify: verify snapshot exists + basic integrity checks
  - backup.complete: emit manifest + persist upgrade state
  - restore.start: validate target + confirm operator intent (guardrails)
  - restore.apply: restore from snapshot(s) / logical dump
  - restore.verify: service health checks + DB consistency checks
  - restore.complete: emit manifest + persist state
- Idempotency requirements:
  - Hook execution must be safely re-runnable (at-least-once). If a backup with the same upgrade_id already exists, installer should detect and reuse it (or require explicit --force-new-backup).
  - Restore must be protected against accidental overwrite (require explicit flag + confirmation + backup reference).

2) What we back up (v1)
- Control-plane DB (primary): snapshot or logical dump depending on environment
- Redwood Private config/state (where stored outside DB) as applicable
- Minimal Kubernetes objects needed to restore control-plane configuration (selected ConfigMaps/Secrets references), without exfiltrating secret material unless explicitly configured.
- Backup metadata: version (from_version, to_version), cluster identity, timestamp, storage backend type, artifact checksums for upgrade bundle (on-prem), KMS key id / encryption context.

3) Storage backend coverage
- VPC (AWS-first for v1):
  - EBS volume snapshots via CSI/EBS APIs (preferred) for stateful components
  - Optional logical DB dump path (fallback / small deployments)
- Kubernetes CSI-generic:
  - VolumeSnapshot API support when a CSI driver implements snapshotting
- On-prem / air-gapped:
  - Default: logical DB dump to a local mounted path (NFS / local persistent volume / customer-provided backup store)
  - Optional: CSI VolumeSnapshot if available (documented as “supported if driver supports snapshots”)

4) Encryption + key management requirements (must-have)
- Backups at rest must be encrypted.
  - AWS EBS snapshots: require encryption enabled; if customer specifies a KMS key, use it; otherwise default to account-managed KMS with explicit audit logging.
  - Logical dumps: encrypt before writing to destination using customer-provided KMS integration when available (KMS/HSM). For air-gapped, support envelope encryption with a locally-managed key (document constraints + operator responsibilities).
- Encryption context should include: cluster_id, environment_id, backup_id, created_at.
- Do not log secret material, credentials, or unredacted encryption context values.

5) Auditability
- Installer must persist:
  - backup_manifest.json (or equivalent) alongside the upgrade plan state
  - restore_manifest.json when restore is executed
  - checksums of produced artifacts (logical dump) or snapshot IDs (EBS/CSI)
- Emit audit log events via control plane where available (start/finish/failure) with correlation_id = upgrade_id.

Acceptance criteria
- Backup hook is invoked automatically for upgrade plans when an upgrade reaches the irreversible boundary (before DB migration step).
- Restore hook can be invoked deterministically via installer rollback command (consumes stored upgrade state, references a known backup_id).
- Coverage:
  - AWS EBS snapshot path implemented and tested in integration (happy path + insufficient IAM perms)
  - Logical DB dump path implemented and tested (happy path + out-of-disk + permission denied)
  - CSI VolumeSnapshot path implemented behind feature detection and documented behavior
- Encryption:
  - EBS snapshot encryption is enforced (fails fast if unencrypted)
  - Logical dumps are encrypted prior to write (configurable; defaults to enabled)
- Documentation notes for operators (internal runbook + doc snippet) includes:
  - how to configure backup destination
  - how to verify backup manifests
  - how to restore safely and verify success

Implementation notes / open questions
- Where to store logical backups by default in VPC installs (S3 vs PVC)? Current proposal:
  - VPC: S3 (preferred) if configured; otherwise PVC path with clear warnings re: durability.
  - On-prem: filesystem path only (operator-managed durability).
- DB type assumptions: Postgres primary. Need to confirm pg_dump compatibility across supported versions and whether we require pg_dump in the installer container or run a Kubernetes Job.
- Maintenance mode requirements: do we require short read-only window for consistency? For v1, propose:
  - For logical dump: enable maintenance mode for control plane UI/API; pause background migrations/jobs; then run dump.
  - For EBS snapshots: rely on filesystem-level consistency + DB checkpoint step if feasible.

References / related work
- Installer PR: sources/github/redwood-private-installer/pr-4850-backup-orchestrator-and-snapshot-hooks.json
- Rollback state machine: ENG-4844 / installer rollback implementation PR-4862
- Preflight check framework: ENG-4829 / installer preflight PR-4834
- Backup/restore strategy doc: sources/confluence/eng-private-deployments/upgrade-and-rollback/backup-and-restore-strategy-private.json
- On-prem bundle constraints: sources/confluence/eng-private-deployments/onprem-packaging/onprem-upgrade-bundle-format.json

Risks
- Snapshot APIs vary widely across CSI drivers; must be explicit about what’s supported and fail with actionable remediation.
- Encryption defaults must not break existing installs unexpectedly; we should provide a migration path (warn for one release, then enforce).
- Logical backup performance could extend maintenance windows for large DBs; need a documented fallback (snapshot) and guidance for sizing/throughput.

Rollout plan
- Beta: enable backup hooks by default for design partners; gather timing + reliability data; run a rollback drill (restore) in staging and one partner environment.
- GA: enforce encryption and block upgrades without a verified backup (unless explicit --skip-backup with risk acknowledgement + approval gate).
comments: 2025-03-07 — Talia Benson (Program Manager): Creating per kickoff. We need backups + deterministic restore hooks before we can claim rollback semantics for Private. Vanessa to drive infra/storage coverage; Michael to advise on DB consistency steps.

2025-03-12 — Vanessa Ortiz: Drafted hook phases proposal (preflight/backups/verify). Biggest decision: VPC default destination (S3 vs PVC). Leaning S3 if configured; otherwise PVC with warning. Will sync with Markus/Fatima re: on-prem constraints.

2025-03-18 — Irene Choi: Security note: must not dump Secrets by default; store references only. For logical dumps, encryption must be on by default. Add explicit guidance for air-gapped key handling and ensure support bundle redaction.

2025-04-02 — Michael Nguyen: For Postgres consistency: recommend issuing CHECKPOINT + short pause of background jobs before snapshot/dump. For logical dump, consider running pg_dump in a K8s Job with a pinned image to avoid host tooling drift.

2025-04-16 — Fatima Noor: On-prem customers vary: some have CSI snapshots, many don’t. We need a fully offline-friendly path that only requires a writable mounted directory and a documented retention procedure. Also: operator wants a single “backup artifact” folder they can rsync/tape.

2025-05-06 — Vanessa Ortiz: Implemented backup orchestrator + snapshot hooks in installer PR-4850. Adds manifest + progress reporting. Next: integrate with upgrade plan so backup runs before DB migration stage; add negative tests (IAM denied, unencrypted snapshot, insufficient disk).

2025-05-19 — Sean Gallagher (SRE): Please make ‘backup.verify’ a hard gate before proceeding. Also add explicit timeout defaults and surface time remaining / next steps in CLI output. We should emit audit events for start/complete/fail with upgrade_id.

2025-06-03 — Naomi Feldman (Security/Compliance): Encryption requirements look right. Add requirement: store KMS key id / encryption context in manifest, but redact any customer identifiers beyond cluster_id/environment_id. Ensure logs don’t include dump file paths if they reveal sensitive mount names.

2025-06-11 — Vanessa Ortiz: Wired backup hook into upgrade plan generator (local branch). Encountered CSI snapshot API differences; implementing feature detection and an explicit error: ‘VolumeSnapshotClass not found’ with remediation. Will document as ‘supported when driver supports snapshots’.

2025-06-18 — Connor O'Brien (Release Eng): Marking as In Review pending: (1) integration test coverage in nightly matrix for AWS EBS path, (2) docs snippet for runbook, (3) security sign-off on default encryption behavior for logical dumps. Targeting private-2025.06 cut.
